subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Manhattan Project: Engineering the Atomic Age
description: One-minute skill: The Manhattan Project: Engineering the Atomic Age.

hook.text: In 1942, the US hired 125,000 workers for a secret project. Most never knew what they were building.

buildup.text: Physicists knew atomic fission was possible. Engineers had to build a factory for material that barely existed.

discovery.text: Oak Ridge, Tennessee, used more electricity than New York City to enrich uranium — one atom at a time.

twist.text: Workers handled radioactive material without knowing the danger. Cancer rates soared decades later.

climax.text: Three years and $2 billion produced two bombs. Engineering solved a physics problem — then ethics caught up.

punchline.text: They engineered the unthinkable. Then it was used.

quiz.question: How much electricity did Oak Ridge use to enrich uranium?
options: About the same as a small Midwestern town
More electricity than the entire city of New York
Roughly half of Tennessee's total power output
